checks.s: The memo identifies the tendered aggregate limit as $5,000,000 and the Playbook § 3.1 requirement as $10,000,000.
The memo identifies the aggregate shortfall as $5,000,000 (50%).
The memo rates the aggregate limit shortfall as Critical risk.
The memo connects the $5,000,000 aggregate limit shortfall to MSA § 11.2, which requires no less than $10,000,000 per claim and aggregate cyber liability insurance.
The memo identifies the tendered per-claim limit as $5,000,000 versus the $10,000,000 requirement in Playbook § 3.1 and MSA § 11.2.
The memo flags the complete absence of Social Engineering Fraud coverage as a separate deviation rated Critical or High.
The memo states that Playbook § 3.1 requires a $1,000,000 Social Engineering Fraud sub-limit and that the tendered policy excludes this coverage entirely.
The memo flags the complete absence of Contingent/Dependent Business Interruption coverage as a separate deviation.
The memo states that Playbook § 3.1 requires a $2,000,000 sub-limit and that the tendered policy excludes this coverage entirely.
The memo identifies the BI & Extra Expense sub-limit as $2,000,000 tendered versus $5,000,000 required by Playbook § 3.1, a $3,000,000 / 60% shortfall.
The memo assigns a risk rating to the BI & Extra Expense sub-limit shortfall.
The memo identifies the Regulatory Defense & Penalties sub-limit as $1,000,000 tendered versus $3,000,000 required by Playbook § 3.1, a $2,000,000 / 67% shortfall.
The memo identifies the PCI-DSS Assessment Coverage sub-limit as $500,000 tendered versus $2,000,000 required by Playbook § 3.1, a $1,500,000 / 75% shortfall.
The memo identifies the Crisis Management / Notification Costs sub-limit as $750,000 tendered versus $2,000,000 required by Playbook § 3.1, a $1,250,000 / 63% shortfall.
The memo identifies the Ransomware / Cyber Extortion sub-limit as $1,000,000 tendered versus $3,000,000 required by Playbook § 3.1, a $2,000,000 / 67% shortfall.
The memo rates Section XII.A (subrogation clause) as a Critical risk to Meridian.

The memo states that the insurer retains full subrogation rights against all service providers, including IT vendors, directly exposing Meridian, and that Playbook § 4 requires a waiver of subrogation in favor of contracted service providers.
The memo states that the subrogation clause conflicts with MSA § 11.4, which requires a mutual waiver of subrogation for all insurance policies maintained under the agreement.
The memo recommends a full waiver-of-subrogation endorsement naming Meridian for the subrogation deviation.
The memo flags the 'Computer System' definition in Section II.F as a Critical or High deviation.

The memo states that the definition is limited to systems 'owned, operated, or leased by the Insured,' excludes third-party cloud infrastructure, and differs from Playbook § 4's requirement to include cloud-hosted environments managed by authorized service providers.
The memo says the narrow 'Computer System' definition is especially significant because Meridian provides cloud-hosted ERP and/or payroll services to Castlegate.
The memo flags Section VI.A's notice period as a deviation, stating that the tendered policy requires claims reported within 30 days of discovery versus the 60-day standard in Playbook § 4.
The memo flags Section VII.D's consent-to-settle / hammer clause as a deviation, stating that the tendered 70/30 hammer differs from Playbook § 4's maximum of 80/20 or softer.
The memo recommends amending the hammer clause to at least 80/20.
The memo flags Section IX.B as a panel counsel deviation and identifies the three pre-approved firms: Rourke Stillman LLP, Hargrove & Ng P.C., and Adler Fenn McCready PLLC.
The memo states that the policy provides no ability to appoint own counsel and that Playbook § 4 requires free choice of counsel upon conflict or regulatory proceeding.
The memo flags Endorsement PIS-E-2024-014 (Insured vs. Insured Exclusion) as a deviation and notes that it lacks the whistleblower and derivative claims carve-back required by Playbook § 5.

The memo flags Endorsement PIS-E-2024-019 (War / Cyber-Terrorism Exclusion) as a deviation, identifying its broad LMA 5567-equivalent language and lack of carve-back for collateral cyber events or passive infrastructure.
The memo states that Playbook § 5 requires LMA 5569 or equivalent wording with a passive-infrastructure carve-back.

The memo flags Section XIV.C as a change-of-control deviation, stating that the tendered policy terminates upon an acquisition/merger exceeding 25% voting equity and provides only a 30-day discovery period.
The memo states that Playbook § 4 requires a 60-day discovery window plus automatic 90-day ERP.

The memo flags Section IV.K as a betterment-exclusion deviation, stating that the tendered policy applies a full exclusion with no percentage threshold and Playbook § 4 permits a deduction only to the extent improvement exceeds 120% of pre-loss functionality.

The memo flags Endorsement PIS-E-2024-022 (Voluntary Shutdown) as a deviation, stating that the tendered sub-limit is $250,000 with a 24-hour waiting period versus Playbook § 3.1's $1,000,000 sub-limit and 8-hour waiting period.
The memo identifies the Privacy/Network Security SIR as $150,000 versus Playbook § 3.2's maximum of $100,000.
The memo identifies the BI waiting period as 16 hours versus Playbook § 3.2's maximum of 8 hours.
The memo identifies the Ransomware SIR as $250,000 versus Playbook § 3.2's maximum of $100,000.
The memo identifies the Regulatory SIR as $150,000 versus Playbook § 3.2's maximum of $75,000.
The memo flags the optional 12-month ERP buy-back as off-market: $187,500 (100% of annual premium) versus the Playbook § 6 benchmark of ≤75% of premium ($140,625), exceeding it by $46,875.
The memo recommends negotiating the optional 12-month ERP buy-back down to 75% of premium or less.
The memo states that the broker estimates increasing the aggregate to $10,000,000 would cost approximately $340,000 annually, an ~81.3% increase from $187,500 per broker-premium-schedule.xlsx Tab 3.
The memo assesses whether the premium increase is proportionate to the risk mitigation.
The memo uses the Playbook § 8 risk-rating scale of Critical / High / Medium / Low and applies an appropriate rating to each deviation.
The memo rates the aggregate limit shortfall and subrogation exposure to Meridian as Critical.
The memo states that the aggregate limit shortfall directly breaches MSA § 11.2, which requires $10M per claim and aggregate cyber insurance.
The memo cross-references MSA § 11.4, which requires a mutual waiver of subrogation, for the subrogation clause deviation.

The memo cross-references MSA § 14.1, stating that Castlegate indemnifies Meridian for data breach/network-security failure losses and that inadequate coverage may impair this indemnification backstop.
The memo's TB&A template header block includes the matter name, reference number MSA-2025-CF-0417, date, attorney Lena Kowalski, and client contact Priya Chandrasekaran.
The memo includes an executive summary section.

The memo includes a structured issues table with columns for Issue Number, Policy Provision Reference, Playbook Requirement Reference, Description of Deviation, Risk Rating, Financial Impact, Recommended Position, and Fallback Position.

The memo includes sections for missing coverages, off-market terms, retention/deductible analysis, ERP analysis, carrier rating assessment, MSA cross-reference compliance, and concluding recommendation.
The redline marks the Declarations page aggregate limit of $5M versus the required $10M with proposed conforming language or commentary.
The redline marks the Declarations page per-claim limit of $5M versus the required $10M with proposed conforming language or commentary.

The redline marks the BI sub-limit ($2M→$5M), Regulatory sub-limit ($1M→$3M), PCI-DSS sub-limit ($500K→$2M), Crisis Management sub-limit ($750K→$2M), Ransomware sub-limit ($1M→$3M), and Voluntary Shutdown sub-limit ($250K→$1M) with proposed conforming language or commentary.
The redline marks the Voluntary Shutdown waiting period change (24h→8h) with proposed conforming language or commentary.

The redline marks all four retention/SIR deviations with proposed conforming language or commentary: Privacy/Network Security ($150K→$100K), BI waiting period (16h→8h), Ransomware ($250K→$100K), and Regulatory ($150K→$75K).
The redline marks Section II.F ('Computer System' definition) with proposed language including cloud-hosted environments managed by authorized service providers.
The redline marks Section VI.A with a proposed notice-period change from 30 days to 60 days.
The redline marks Section VII.D with a proposed hammer-clause change from 70/30 to 80/20 or softer.
The redline marks Section IX.B with a proposed addition of free choice of counsel upon conflict or regulatory proceeding.
The redline marks Section XII.A with a proposed waiver-of-subrogation endorsement naming Meridian.
The redline marks Section IV.K with a proposed amendment limiting the betterment deduction to improvements exceeding 120% of pre-loss functionality.
The redline marks Section XIV.C with proposed changes to a 60-day discovery window and automatic 90-day ERP.
The redline marks Endorsement PIS-E-2024-014 with a proposed addition of a whistleblower and derivative claims carve-back.
The redline marks Endorsement PIS-E-2024-019 with a proposed replacement of LMA 5567-equivalent language with LMA 5569 or equivalent wording that includes a passive-infrastructure carve-back.
The redline marks Endorsement PIS-E-2024-022 with a proposed sub-limit change from $250K to $1M and waiting-period change from 24h to 8h.
The memo assesses Pinnacle's AM Best rating of A- (Excellent), Financial Size Category VIII, against the carrier standards in Playbook § 7.
Every deviation in the structured issues table has both a Recommended Position stating the ideal outcome per playbook and a Fallback Position stating an acceptable alternative.
The memo notes that Castlegate expressed willingness to discuss endorsement modifications subject to commercially reasonable premium impact, per castlegate-policy-transmittal-email.eml.
The memo calibrates its recommended positions to use Castlegate's stated willingness to negotiate.
The memo identifies the automatic 60-day ERP as conforming with the playbook.
The memo flags the optional 12-month ERP cost as off-market, stating it is 100% of premium versus the Playbook § 6 benchmark of ≤75%.
The memo separately analyzes the absence of an automatic 90-day ERP triggered by change of control against Playbook § 4's requirement for a 60-day discovery window plus automatic 90-day ERP.
The memo's concluding recommendation clearly assesses whether the tendered policy satisfies Meridian's playbook and MSA requirements.
The concluding recommendation identifies which deviations are deal-critical and must be resolved before the April 1, 2025 MSA execution date and which can be addressed at renewal.
The redline proposes adding Social Engineering Fraud coverage as a new endorsement with a minimum $1,000,000 sub-limit per Playbook § 3.1.
The redline proposes adding Contingent/Dependent Business Interruption coverage as a new endorsement with a minimum $2,000,000 sub-limit per Playbook § 3.1.
The memo states that the MSA has a 3-year total contract value of $4,860,000 and annual value of $1,620,000 per msa-2025-cf-0417-draft.docx.
The memo relates coverage adequacy to the scale of the engagement and explains why the $5M aggregate is insufficient relative to deal size and Meridian's downstream liability exposure.
The memo identifies Monica Chu at Whitfield Brokerage Partners as the broker contact for policy amendments and endorsement requests.
The memo notes that Pinnacle is a surplus lines insurer domiciled in Connecticut and admitted in 38 states per the policy.
The memo assesses the implications of Pinnacle's surplus lines status for policy enforceability or guarantee-fund protection.
